answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates immediate churn pressure on SMB accounts, but memory_73 and exp_73 clearly show that promotional pricing drives short-term acquisition at the cost of 12% retention loss and cohort survival failure—unsustainable against the primary objective. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well on established customers but won't address active churn. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB crisis. Signup simplification (memory_31) has already been deployed. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the strategic alternative: it improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action, building product stickiness and perceived value. In a price-war scenario, increasing product adoption velocity and demonstrating value faster may reduce price sensitivity and churn more durably than matching the discount. This preserves the ability to test promotional pricing later if activation messaging proves insufficient, and aligns with the long-term qualified revenue objective by targeting retention and product-led differentiation rather than race-to-bottom acquisition.
